text: I'm Anatoly, co founder of Solana Labs and Solana itself. I got into crypto in 2017. I was in Cafe Soleil with Stephen, one of the co founders, and I had two coffees and a beer and that didn't sit with me. So I was up till 4 in the morning because I couldn't sleep. And I had this like eureka moment. In Bitcoin, if you have two bitcoin block producers that make a block at the same time, you have a fork and the network has to figure out what the next step is. And that's noisy. You're effectively dropping data in radio. These folks came up with this thing called time division, multiple access tdma. You give each tower a clock and you let them alternate by time so they never transmit at the same time. I was like, oh, I can build TDMA but in blockchain and therefore it can be much, much faster, get the same speed up as you do in radio. And that was enough to kind of dislodge me from what I was doing. And my wife, we had a kid and we're both working. Her view was, I can't do all three. I can't have a job, be a father and do a major side project. I have to pick two, and the child is mandatory. I couldn't skip out on that one. So it was between either go full time, be a founder, or drop it. And luckily, with her encouragement, I took the plunge. I started thinking, what's the point of this thing? And I immediately thought that trading would be the key use case. I wanted to build a product that could capture value, that has some utility use case that people cared about. All the data is publicly available and you have this transparent implementation of how it's propagated around the world. You know how everything works, everything's open source. So I feel like it would create an open and fair environment to create markets. It's pretty amazing how just because of the guarantees it provides, that reduces business risk and people can build on top of that. It's just really hard to believe how many founders can go start a business and get to product market fit and make revenue just because we built this message bus.
